activeForm: Routing Pl/t transpile helpers through one stderr-aware helper
description:
FILED s403 (Fable) from the s402 review request §5 (Opus 5 asked whether to file).

~20 Pl/t/*.t helpers run `$pl2cl $file 2>&1` and write the result straight into
the .lisp they then load — transpile stderr becomes Lisp source.  Today nothing
drops in those snippets (gate green), but the day one does, the row fails with a
READER error instead of the drop line, and a transpile ERROR is equally opaque.
This is why the two blanket $SIG{__WARN__} silencers deleted in s402 existed.

SHAPE (rule 11 — one helper, not 20 edits): the shared transpile helper in
Pl/t/PCLCore.pm captures stderr SEPARATELY (never into the .lisp), and
  - a stderr line matching the FIXED prefix `PCL: statement dropped` FAILS the
    row, diag = the line (a dropped statement inside a gate snippet is a
    compiler bug the gate must catch — the gate becomes a drop detector for its
    own snippets; rule-12 spirit);
  - a nonzero pl2cl exit FAILS the row, diag = stderr;
  - other stderr (warnings) is passed through with diag, row verdict unchanged.
Then port the ~20 copies onto that helper (list them with
`grep -ln '2>&1' Pl/t/*.t`), each in the same commit as its measurement:
`prove --timer` before/after must be identical per file.  Any row that goes RED
in the port is a real drop that was hiding — fix or file, never re-silence.

Not urgent (the failure mode is loud, not silent): filler after session B.


DONE s406 (d5d88c8).  PCLCore::transpile (judges: drop announcement or nonzero exit FAILS the row, other stderr is a diag) + PCLCore::transpile_raw (judges nothing, for rows that assert on the transpiler's diagnostics).  60 sites in 38 files ported.  It caught one hider at once: transpile-test-10.t's `grep { … }->{a}` row read pl2cl's perl-shaped death out of the merged stream; it now uses transpile_raw.  Gate unchanged 146/5346, 217 s vs 215 s.
subject: ~20 Pl/t helpers merge transpile stderr INTO the .lisp (`2>&1`) — route through ONE shared helper that FAILS the row on a drop announcement
